entities.summary: John of Segovia, or in Spanish Juan de Segovia, was a Castilian prelate and theologian who played a prominent role in the Council of Basle. Born in unknown circumstances, he spent his early career in the service of the Catholic Church, rising to become a key advisor to the Bishop of Burgos. He was in touch with the leading humanists of his day, such as Nicholas of Cusa, and spent the last years of his life in exile in Savoy, where he commissioned an accurate translation of the Koran into Spanish, which he then translated into Latin. This translation, known as the 'Corán en castellano', was a groundbreaking work that helped to popularize Islamic scholarship among Christian Europeans. John of Segovia's significance lies in his role as a mediator between Christianity and Islam, as well as his contributions to the development of theology and biblical studies in medieval Europe. His legacy can be seen in the many scholars and theologians who followed in his footsteps, including the famous Dominican friar, Albertus Magnus.
